texts.085d99c17dae: Peripheral vascular disease (PVD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality. Patients with PVD often have significant medical conditions, such as coronary heart disease, high blood pressure and impaired function of the blood vessels and possibly stiffened arteries. Data concerning arterial stiffness in patients with PVD is limited, but stiffness predicts cardiovascular events in other patient groups. The aim of this study is to determine whether arterial stiffness predicts outcome in patients with PVD. We believe that a better understanding of vascular changes in PVD patients may eventually help us in treating patients with PVD and also in determining the risk for the future cardiovascular events, but this study will not provide any direct benefit for those taking part.
